issues.description: Enabled programmatic resolve receives untrusted configuration/catalogue data but checks its 1 MiB configuration_bytes bound only after canonical() fully serializes each arbitrary object into a newly allocated string and bytes (tools/skill_recommendations.py lines 27-28, 328). An 8 MiB input caused 18,875,935 bytes of new traced allocation before rejection, despite a 1,048,576-byte limit. A much larger or deeply nested host-supplied value can exhaust the process before the prescribed bounded refusal. CLI file reads are bounded, but the documented programmatic host interface is not. Add a bounded preflight/streaming serialization approach for untrusted in-memory objects, including large strings, nesting and cycles; preserve disabled/declined no-read behavior and add a discriminating negative control.

required_fixes: Bound work and intermediate allocation before or during serialization of untrusted programmatic config/catalogue inputs; reject oversized/nested/cyclic structures predictably, add adversarial tests and rerun affected evidence.
review_checks: All 12 scoped product files match the source-freeze SHA256 map and approved contract scope.
Focused resolver and filesystem boundary suites exited 0 in separate validator captures.
Code inspection found no input-selected executable, network, installation, or host acceptance path; disabled/declined return before package observation.
Programmatic trusted verifier must match exact binding, release flag and supported mapping; default CLI has no verifier.
Descriptor walks apply no-follow, identity and operation-wide entry/directory controls; host docs require revalidation before later entrypoint load.
Fixture version and derived anchor changes are scoped by approved mechanical amendment.
limitations: No independent Evaluator QA, DS qualification, release, compatibility or publication claim.
